expectations.text: Shows evidence of reading the existing context files (references Orders and/or Customers by name or documented definition)
expectations.evidence: Summarises Orders (core/promising) and Customers (supporting) and the existing identity link.

expectations.text: Asks whether loyalty points should be a new context/area or live inside an existing one (Customers or Orders)
expectations.evidence: '**Q:** Is loyalty points a distinct area... or a feature folded into Orders or Customers?'

expectations.text: Uses the Q:/Recommendation format with a concrete recommendation
expectations.evidence: Q:/Recommendation: 'Make it its own area' with lifecycle reasoning.

expectations.text: Does not re-ask about file structure, since context files already exist
expectations.evidence: Goes straight to grilling; no file-structure question.

expectations.text: Uses plain business language with NO DDD jargon in the user-facing text
expectations.evidence: Plain language ('its own area', 'competitive edge'); no DDD jargon.

expectations.text: If it proposes a relationship label, it uses only canonical DDD patterns (Customer-Supplier, ACL, Open Host Service, etc.) and does NOT invent labels such as 'Publisher-Subscriber'
expectations.evidence: Proposes no label and invents none; mentions Orders 'never has to know loyalty exists' (deferred to YAML).

expectations.text: Keeps implementation details (DB schemas, points-ledger/table design) out — artifacts stay glossaries, not specs
expectations.evidence: Stays at area/ownership; no ledger or table design.
